clue.text: Feeling aroused by crossing my path in Surrey briefly

indicators.note: the words my path are placed in the middle of the short form for Surrey

parts.note: Sy is the standard abbreviation for the English county of Surrey

indicators.note: aroused means stirred up, so the two letters of my are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone feels stirred up after a stranger crosses their path in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south of London, abbreviated Sy; 'aroused' stirs MY into YM, and 'in' puts YM plus PATH between the letters of SY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sympathy is a feeling of compassion or fellow-feeling for another person.

clue.text: Savant I left inside getting a feed

indicators.note: the letters of I and left are set within the word for savant

parts.note: a sage is a wise or learned person, a savant
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scholar leaves the house and finds something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Silage is fermented grass or fodder stored to feed livestock.

clue.text: Possibly on edge with such violence

parts.note: may expresses possibility, as in 'it may rain'
a hem is the folded edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone already on edge might turn violent.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is wild disorder and violent destruction.

clue.text: A weight on a New York State capital

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
taken as written

explanation.surface: A heavy load lands on the capital of New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: Albany is the seat of government of New York State.

clue.text: Going home to stay in?

definitions.meaning: read literally, bound for the house, heading homewards
unable to leave one's home, confined indoors

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means heading for the house; as one word it describes someone confined indoors.

clue.text: Rock-dweller writing about us to the Spanish

indicators.note: the manuscript abbreviation goes round the word us

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
taken as written
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A climber writes a note about the group before heading off to Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A mussel is a shellfish that clings to rocks on the shore.

clue.text: Cannot take us in, being impractical

indicators.note: the word for cannot takes in the word us, so it holds it

parts.note: unable means cannot do something
taken as written

explanation.surface: A host apologises that they cannot put us up because it is not practical.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unusable cannot be put to practical use.

clue.text: Talking picture in the por trait gallery?

definitions.text: Talking picture in the por trait gallery?

parts.words: Talking picture in the por trait gallery?
parts.note: not a film with sound but a portrait so true to life it seems about to talk

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a film playing among the paintings of an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talking picture' suggests an early sound film; the portrait gallery shows it is a painted portrait. The clue prints 'por trait', a typesetting split of portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifelike portrait is so faithful to its sitter that it seems ready to talk.

clue.text: See 7
Song relating to a lazy character

parts.note: a lay is an old word for a song or ballad
about means concerning or relating to

explanation.surface: A ballad tells the story of an idle person.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout is an idle person who avoids work.

clue.text: Be in luck in Germany

definitions.note: the definition points to a place found in Germany, a city

indicators.note: the word be is put inside the word luck

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wish for good fortune while travelling in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is the container signal; the second belongs to the definition: a city in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Lübeck is a Hanseatic port city in northern Germany.

clue.text: Island jumper worn by sailors

definitions.meaning: one of the Channel Islands off the coast of Normandy
a thick knitted woollen sweater traditionally worn by fishermen and seamen

explanation.definitionFit: It names a Channel Island and also the oiled-wool sweater that originated there and is worn by seafarers.

clue.text: Pointer around the menagerie takes the biscuit

indicators.note: the word for pointer is wrapped around the word for menagerie

parts.note: a pin can serve as a pointer, as on a map
Noah's ark held a menagerie of animals two by two

explanation.surface: A dog at the zoo behaves outrageously, which really takes the biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes the biscuit' is a British idiom for being the most outrageous; here 'takes' is a link. Parkin is a ginger oatmeal cake or biscuit from northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkin is a Yorkshire ginger and oatmeal cake, also made as biscuits.

clue.text: Poetry of Burns, say

parts.note: Burns looks like the Scottish poet, but read as the verb it suggests verse that ignites, playful humorous poetry

explanation.surface: An example of the poetry of Robert Burns, the Scottish poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet; but 'burns' also means catches fire, giving a pun on the playful kind of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Light verse is humorous, playful poetry, the reverse of serious verse.

clue.text: Noble Roman finding colour a sin

indicators.note: the letters are found by casting them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Roman aristocrat thinks that colour is sinful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finding' signals that COLOUR A SIN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriolanus is the Roman patrician general of legend and of Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Takesbits of horse

definitions.meaning: to grab or steal something quickly
simple jointed bits placed in a horse's mouth

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means steals or grabs; as a plural noun it means simple bridle mouthpieces.

clue.text: Female garments collectively to which the French tout gives effect

definitions.meaning: a woman's matching outfit worn together

definitions.text: to which the French tout gives effect
definitions.meaning: the French phrase 'tout ...' means the overall effect or general impression

explanation.definitionFit: It is a coordinated outfit of clothes, and in the French phrase with tout it means the overall impression.

clue.text: Enclosure where the stakes are high

definitions.text: Enclosure where the stakes are high

parts.words: Enclosure where the stakes are high
parts.note: not a gambling den with big bets but a fence of tall posts

explanation.surface: A casino room where gamblers place big bets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stakes are high' sounds like a big-money gamble; the stakes are wooden posts.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a defensive barrier of upright timber posts.

clue.text: Fractionally short of being all there

definitions.text: Fractionally short of being all there

parts.words: Fractionally short of being all there
parts.note: 'not all there' means a bit simple, but here the shortfall is a literal fraction just under one whole

explanation.surface: Someone is not quite all there mentally.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety per cent is a fraction just below the whole.

clue.text: Safer river found in Canada

definitions.note: the definition points to something located in Canada, a river

indicators.note: to found metal is to cast it, so the letters are recast

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds a safer river to travel in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' signals that SAFER is recast as FRASE, then R for river follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fraser is the longest river in British Columbia, Canada.

clue.text: He comes in to make Margaret happy

indicators.note: the man's name is set inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A man arrives to cheer Margaret up.
explanation.definitionFit: Gareth is a man's given name, so it can stand for any 'he'.

clue.text: Waldteufel's choice for a waltz

parts.note: the composer Emile Waldteufel wrote a famous waltz named after people gliding on ice

explanation.surface: A composer picks a subject for a new waltz.
explanation.walkthrough: Emile Waldteufel was a French composer whose best-known piece is 'Les Patineurs', The Skaters' Waltz.
explanation.definitionFit: Waldteufel's famous waltz is dedicated to people gliding on an ice rink.

clue.text: Charge exorbitantly for a woollen coat

explanation.definitionFit: It means to overcharge someone, and also a sheep's coat of wool.

clue.text: Work too hard? Certainly open to question

parts.note: overt means plainly open and undisguised
to ask is to question

explanation.surface: A colleague wonders whether they are overdoing it, which is clearly debatable.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtask is to give someone more work than they can manage.

clue.text: An African party, anyway

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party

indicators.note: any way means the letters may be arranged in any way at all

explanation.surface: An African political party, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' signals that ANY is rearranged to YAN after LIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A Libyan is a native of Libya in North Africa.

clue.text: Survey with a view to profit

definitions.text: Survey with a view to profit

parts.words: Survey with a view to profit
parts.note: to explore ground for gold or minerals in the hope of making money

explanation.surface: A surveyor looks over land hoping to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospecting is searching land for valuable minerals to exploit.

clue.text: Land in a corner of Paradise?

parts.note: SW, south-west, is one corner of the compass
Eden is the garden of paradise in Genesis

explanation.surface: A plot of land tucked into one corner of heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass corners are NE, NW, SE and SW; here it is south-west.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian country, a land in northern Europe.

clue.text: Dutiful-looking Customs officer

parts.note: an official whose duty is looking through travellers' luggage, and who collects duty

explanation.surface: A customs official who appears conscientious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutiful-looking' seems to mean appearing conscientious, but it means looking for goods liable to duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A searcher was a customs officer who examined goods and luggage.
